Subject: Follow-up: post-demo briefing — SLOs, model fit, and next ops asks

Thanks again for taking the time today, Tim — appreciated the candid discussion. This thread is a short capture of what we heard, what we think the next technical checkpoints are, and suggested next steps so we stay aligned heading into procurement.

Key pain points you shared:
- End-users see inconsistently long tail latency on inference requests (esp. >2s on certain prompt shapes).
- Cost unpredictability at peak hours due to bursty traffic and lack of efficient batching.
- Strict data locality and audit requirements for PII extraction flow (on-prem / VPC preferred).

Goals we mapped to during the call:
- 95th percentile latency <= 300ms per token for production critical routes (summary + entity extraction).
- Monthly cost target not to exceed $X / 1M tokens for baseline traffic; need to refine with your QPS curves.
- SOC2-style evidence for audit trail and cross-region access control.

Technical notes / constraints we captured:
- Expected request distribution: 60% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 30% medium (128–512), 10% long (>512) — will follow up to confirm with sample traces.
- Model family preference: open Llama-family derivative or our recommended quantized 7B variant for cost/latency tradeoffs; will validate on your test set.
- Deployment topology: private VPC with dedicated GPUs (we recommend Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering); automatic fallback to hosted-in-region variant for burst capacity.

Immediate asks (owner/comment):
1) Apex: share a 48-hour representative traffic sample (timestamps + prompt lengths) — procurement/ops team can sanitize PII (Tim)
2) Redwood: run a quick baseline quantization test against a 1k-sample set to surface expected P95 latency and token cost (Marissa)
3) Both: confirm a list of endpoints that must be air-gapped vs. those allowed to hit hosted fallback (Tim/Procurement)

Attachments: Apex security questionnaire (you mentioned procurement would attach), and I’ve included a draft mutual action plan for procurement (redwood_mutual_action_plan_draft.md).

Next meeting suggestion: ops deep-dive with your infra lead + our ops engineer next Wednesday 11/10 at 10:00 PT — I’ll hold tentative time unless you prefer morning on the 11th.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Tim — quick technical summary from our side based on the sample shapes you described on the call + the latency targets Hannah listed. This is meant to be a pragmatic starting point for the ops deep-dive.

Summary of recommendations:
1) Model selection and quantization
- Start with a 7B quantized open model (8-bit or 4-bit per your accuracy tolerance) for the summary + entity routes. 7B hit a good cost/latency sweet spot in our benchmarks.
- Reserve a 13B variant as a fallthrough for complex prompts (we can route using heuristic length/complexity).

2) Serving topology
- Private VPC deployment: dedicated GPU cluster (NVIDIA H100 or equivalent) behind a regional ingress gateway.
- Autoscaling policy: maintain a baseline worker pool sized for 95th percentile steady-state QPS; allow fast horizontal scale-up triggered by queue depth and a capacity-buffer SLO.
- Burst fallback: configurable route to Redwood hosted-in-region pool with throttled request burst to avoid cold starts.

3) Latency optimization levers
- Continuous batching with knobbed max_delay_ms (start at 10ms) and dynamic batch sizing by prompt-length class.
- KV-cache for repeated prefixes and aggressive prefix caching on the summary route.
- Model compilation kernels tuned for target sequence lengths (we’ll precompile common variants).

4) Observability & auditing
- Token-level cost & latency traces per route, request-id correlation with your logs.
- Audit export to your S3 (or on-prem) with 12-month retention; we’ll surface the SHA256 of exported bundles for immutability checks.

Immediate technical asks from Redwood (so we can prepare a staging benchmark):
- A 1k-sample set representative of the top three route types (Hannah / Tim to coordinate).
- Your QPS distribution and any expected growth spikes (hourly and weekly).
- Confirmation on whether PCI/PHI flows need to remain fully air-gapped (if yes, we’ll scope an on-prem cartridge).

I ran a quick local quantized pass against a small sample you provided during the demo — attached latency samples are illustrative (apex_latency_samples.csv). P95 for the 7B quantized baseline was ~220ms on a dedicated H100-like worker with batching (10ms delay). Expect variance once we run with your real traffic.

Happy to walk through this on the ops call next week.

Cheers — Marissa
Marissa Cole
